title: Registered Common Land

sections.heading: What this means
sections.content: This area is registered as common land under the Commons Registration Act 1965 or Commons Act 2006. It is almost certainly owned — typically by a local council, private individual, or a body such as the National Trust.

sections.heading: What you can do
sections.content: You have the right to roam on registered common land under the Countryside and Rights of Way Act 2000. This means you can walk, climb, and engage in other forms of open-air recreation. You do not need the landowner's permission.

sections.heading: What you cannot do
sections.content: You cannot acquire ownership of registered common land through adverse possession or any other mechanism in most circumstances. The rights of commoners and the public access framework protect this land from individual acquisition.

sections.heading: Village green registration
sections.content: If you believe this or nearby land has been used by local people for recreation for 20 or more years without permission, it may be eligible for registration as a town or village green. This is a community process that protects the land from development — it does not transfer ownership.

confidence_statement: High — that this is registered common land. The Natural England dataset is updated and nationally consistent.
